RC5.gate1_irp_source: IrpTransmogrifier IrpProtocols.xml @c945e76 L2101-L2103 (verbatim), whose documentation names Philips as the protocol's creator. Corroborated by probonopd/irdb, which names RC5 for the Meridian System Remote and Surround Processor (device 19, function 0-127), and by a Flipper-IRDB code set for the Meridian 562/565 whose 48 frames all decode as this layout
RC5.gate2a_structural_vector: Flipper-IRDB@d126fb1b6f1e _Converted_/Pronto/M/Meridian/562+565.ir -- a converted Pronto code set for the Meridian 562 and 565, not vendored here (see tests/vectors/CITATIONS.md). All 48 frames are reproduced by this encoder from the address, command and toggle bit they decode to: 24 end on a mark and 24 on a space, 23 use the extended command range, both toggle states occur. Weaker than a published table, because a capture carries instrument bias and its provenance upstream is unstated

Pioneer-2Part.gate1_irp_source: IrpTransmogrifier IrpProtocols.xml @c945e76 L2060 (verbatim; identical in the 1.2.14 release, L2041). Its documentation describes the intro as the 'normal' signal (D0, F0) and the repeat as the one determined by D and F. Plain `Pioneer` (one frame, ^108m) is not registered: every database code sends two frames
Pioneer-2Part.gate2a_structural_vector: IrpTransmogrifier src/test/teaserfiles/PioneerMix2.ict @c945e76 -- two IrScope hardware captures of a Pioneer receiver ('Setup' and 'Return') that its PioneerMix2.exp decodes as Pioneer-2Part {D0=170,F0=91,D=175,F=36} and {...,F=34}; the excerpts are in tests/vectors/irpt_teaser_japan.json. A capture carries instrument bias, so this verifies the ratios, the field layout and the bit order of all four bytes (D0, ~D0, F0, ~F0 and D, ~D, F, ~F), not absolute durations, and never the idle gaps

JVC.gate1_irp_source: IrpTransmogrifier IrpProtocols.xml @c945e76 L1207 (verbatim; identical in the 1.2.14 release, L1207). Its documentation states JVC has a lead-in on the first frame only and cites JVC's own remote-code document (support.jvc.com/consumer/support/documents/RemoteCodes.pdf)
JVC.gate2a_structural_vector: IrpTransmogrifier src/test/teaserfiles/JVC.ict @c945e76 -- an IrScope file of D=5, F=0..23 that its JVC.exp decodes as JVC {D=5,F=n}; each signal is a 36-duration frame with a lead-in followed by a 34-duration frame without one, exactly this encoder's intro and repeat. Its durations are exact multiples of 525 us, so it reads as generated rather than measured: it verifies the frame shapes and bit order, not absolute timings and not the idle gaps (excerpts in tests/vectors/irpt_teaser_japan.json)
